# Tank Mate Match

> A tank-mate checker for common freshwater aquarium animals. Every range is tied to a named source, and the result says why.

The canonical site is https://tankmatematch.com (apex, no www). Facts are written in the HTML of each species and tank-mate page, with the source named on the page. The set includes freshwater fish and invertebrates. The checker itself runs in the browser. This file was generated from the species records on 2026-10-30.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://tankmatematch.com): Checker embedded on the home page, plus links to every species.
- [Tank mate checker](https://tankmatematch.com/checker): Compare two or more species. The selection is stored in the URL and can be saved in the browser, or on an account when email sign-in is configured.
- [Species index](https://tankmatematch.com/species): The 325 freshwater animals in this version.
- [How a verdict is reached](https://tankmatematch.com/methodology): Sources, disagreements, and the Compatible / Caution / Not compatible rules.
- [About](https://tankmatematch.com/about): What the site is for.
- [Privacy](https://tankmatematch.com/privacy): Optional email sign-in. The email is used only for sign-in and saved tanks. Without it, saved tanks stay in this browser. Vercel Web Analytics records anonymous page views.
- [Affiliate disclosure](https://tankmatematch.com/affiliate-disclosure): No affiliate links or ads in this version.

- [Spike-topped apple snail](https://tankmatematch.com/species/spike-topped-apple-snail) (Pomacea diffusa): 64.4–82.4 °F, pH not stated. [Tank mates](https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/spike-topped-apple-snail).
- [Giant apple snail](https://tankmatematch.com/species/giant-apple-snail) (Pomacea maculata): 59.4–97.9 °F, pH 4–10.5. [Tank mates](https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/giant-apple-snail).
- [Florida apple snail](https://tankmatematch.com/species/florida-apple-snail) (Pomacea paludosa): 64.4–82.4 °F, pH not stated. [Tank mates](https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/florida-apple-snail).
- [Indian apple snail](https://tankmatematch.com/species/indian-apple-snail) (Pila globosa): 64.4–82.4 °F, pH not stated. [Tank mates](https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/indian-apple-snail).
- [Quilted melania](https://tankmatematch.com/species/quilted-melania) (Tarebia granifera): 32–117.5 °F, pH not stated. [Tank mates](https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/quilted-melania).
- [Chinese mystery snail](https://tankmatematch.com/species/chinese-mystery-snail) (Cipangopaludina chinensis): 32–86 °F, pH 6.5–8.4. [Tank mates](https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/chinese-mystery-snail).
- [Faucet snail](https://tankmatematch.com/species/faucet-snail) (Bithynia tentaculata): temperature not stated, pH 6.6–8.4. [Tank mates](https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/faucet-snail).
- [Asian clam](https://tankmatematch.com/species/asian-clam) (Corbicula fluminea): 35.6–86 °F, pH not stated. [Tank mates](https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/asian-clam).
- [New Zealand mudsnail](https://tankmatematch.com/species/new-zealand-mudsnail) (Potamopyrgus antipodarum): 32–93.2 °F, pH not stated. [Tank mates](https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/new-zealand-mudsnail).
- [Red swamp crayfish](https://tankmatematch.com/species/red-swamp-crayfish) (Procambarus clarkii): 69.8–80.6 °F, pH 5.8–10. [Tank mates](https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/red-swamp-crayfish).
- [Redclaw crayfish](https://tankmatematch.com/species/redclaw-crayfish) (Cherax quadricarinatus): 73.4–87.8 °F, pH 6.5–8. [Tank mates](https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/redclaw-crayfish).
- [Marbled crayfish](https://tankmatematch.com/species/marbled-crayfish) (Procambarus virginalis): 64.4–77 °F, pH not stated. [Tank mates](https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/marbled-crayfish).
- [Mexican dwarf crayfish](https://tankmatematch.com/species/mexican-dwarf-crayfish) (Cambarellus patzcuarensis): 50–78.8 °F, pH not stated. [Tank mates](https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/mexican-dwarf-crayfish).

## Species records

### Betta (Betta splendens)

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/betta
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/betta
- Temperature: 22–30 °C (72–86 °F)
- pH: 6–8
- Hardness: 1–15 dGH
- Adult size: 70 mm (2.8 in)
- Minimum tank: 11 US gal
- Minimum group: 1
- Care: moderate
- Verified: 2026-10-30
- Summary: The betta in a shop cup is Betta splendens, a labyrinth fish from still water in central Thailand, almost always an ornamental strain rather than the wild fish. Seriously Fish's current profile is blunt about the housing: one fish, a tank with a real footprint, and no trailing fins in the same water. A jar is not a minimum. It is the setup the source tells you to reject.
- Sources:
  - Seriously Fish: https://www.seriouslyfish.com/species/betta-splendens/
  - FishBase: https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Betta-splendens.html
- Size pages: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/betta/10-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/betta/20-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/betta/29-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/betta/40-gallon

### Neon tetra (Paracheirodon innesi)

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/neon-tetra
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/neon-tetra
- Temperature: 21–25 °C (70–77 °F)
- pH: 4–7.5
- Hardness: 1–12 dGH
- Adult size: 30 mm (1.2 in)
- Minimum tank: 14 US gal
- Minimum group: 8
- Care: easy
- Verified: 2026-10-30
- Summary: Neon tetras are cooler, softer-water fish than the 'community tank at 78°F' habit assumes. Seriously Fish keeps them at 21–25°C (70–77°F), in a school of at least eight, in a tank with a 60 cm base. The colour is real. So is the run of weak, commercially bred stock, and so is the mix-up between an untreatable microsporidian and ordinary columnaris.
- Sources:
  - Seriously Fish: https://www.seriouslyfish.com/species/paracheirodon-innesi/
  - FishBase: https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Paracheirodon-innesi.html
- Size pages: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/neon-tetra/10-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/neon-tetra/20-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/neon-tetra/29-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/neon-tetra/40-gallon

### Guppy (Poecilia reticulata)

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/guppy
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/guppy
- Temperature: 17–28 °C (63–82 °F)
- pH: 7–8.5
- Hardness: 8–30 dGH
- Adult size: 60 mm (2.4 in)
- Minimum tank: 11 US gal
- Minimum group: not stated
- Care: easy
- Verified: 2026-10-30
- Summary: A guppy is a hard-water livebearer, Poecilia reticulata, and the fish in the shop is an ornamental male or female, not the short-finned wild animal. Seriously Fish is specific about the water: moderately hard or harder, alkaline, and not a soft blackwater tank for the long term. The same profile is specific about fins. Do not keep them with fin nippers. A male betta is the case this site refuses outright, because those fins read as a rival.
- Sources:
  - Seriously Fish: https://www.seriouslyfish.com/species/poecilia-reticulata/
  - FishBase: https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Poecilia-reticulata.html
- Size pages: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/guppy/10-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/guppy/20-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/guppy/29-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/guppy/40-gallon

### Bronze corydoras (Osteogaster aenea)

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/bronze-corydoras
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/bronze-corydoras
- Temperature: 21–27 °C (70–81 °F)
- pH: 6–8
- Hardness: 2–15 dGH
- Adult size: 75 mm (3 in)
- Minimum tank: 19 US gal
- Minimum group: 4
- Care: easy
- Verified: 2026-10-30
- Summary: The bronze cory in a shop is sold as Corydoras aeneus and currently stands as Osteogaster aenea on Seriously Fish, which followed a 2024 split of the old genus. The profile is frank that the fish in the bags are commercial animals of unclear identity. What is clear, and what this page uses, is the husbandry: a group, a long footprint, fine substrate, and food that is actually offered to them. They are not a cleanup crew.
- Sources:
  - Seriously Fish: https://www.seriouslyfish.com/species/corydoras-aeneus/
  - FishBase: https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Corydoras-aeneus.html
- Size pages: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/bronze-corydoras/10-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/bronze-corydoras/20-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/bronze-corydoras/40-gallon

### Cherry shrimp (Neocaridina davidi)

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/cherry-shrimp
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/cherry-shrimp
- Temperature: 14–29 °C (57.2–84.2 °F)
- pH: 6.5–8
- Hardness: not stated
- Adult size: 40 mm (1.6 in)
- Minimum tank: No gallon or length minimum in the sources read for this record. Namaei Kohal and coauthors held juveniles in 80 L aquaria and later females in 30 L aquaria. Those are study tanks, not a published minimum, so they are not used as one.
- Minimum group: not stated
- Care: unrated
- Verified: 2026-10-30
- Summary: Cherry shrimp, Neocaridina davidi, are small atyid shrimp. The red ones are a colour form. The limits that matter in a community tank are not a secret pH window. Adults reach about 20–25 mm on average and 40 mm at the outside, and a fish that eats small invertebrates will eat them. The temperature band in the captive literature is wide. The predation problem is not.
- Sources:
  - Klotz et al. 2013: http://www.aquaticinvasions.net/2013/AI_2013_3_Klotz_etal.pdf
  - Namaei Kohal et al. 2018: https://doi.org/10.1007/s10811-017-1220-5
  - USFWS ERSS, 2025: https://www.fws.gov/sites/default/files/documents/2025-06/ecological-risk-screening-summary-cherry-shrimp-june-2025.pdf
- Size pages: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/cherry-shrimp/10-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/cherry-shrimp/20-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/cherry-shrimp/29-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/cherry-shrimp/40-gallon

### Platy (Xiphophorus maculatus)

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/platy
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/platy
- Temperature: 20–26 °C (68–79 °F)
- pH: 7–8.2
- Hardness: 10–30 dGH
- Adult size: 50 mm (2 in)
- Minimum tank: 14 US gal
- Minimum group: not stated
- Care: beginner
- Verified: 2026-10-30
- Summary: A platy is Xiphophorus maculatus, a livebearer from the Atlantic slope of Mexico and northern Central America. It is not a swordtail, and Seriously Fish is clear that the males lack the sword and the attitude that comes with some Xiphophorus. The non-negotiable part is the water. Moderately hard or harder, pH at or above neutral. Soft blackwater is where this species fails, however peaceful it is.
- Sources:
  - Seriously Fish: https://www.seriouslyfish.com/species/xiphophorus-maculatus/
  - FishBase: https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Xiphophorus-maculatus.html
- Size pages: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/platy/10-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/platy/20-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/platy/29-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/platy/40-gallon

### Zebra danio (Danio rerio)

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/zebra-danio
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/zebra-danio
- Temperature: 18–25 °C (64–77 °F)
- pH: 6–8
- Hardness: 5–20 dGH
- Adult size: 50 mm (2 in)
- Minimum tank: 21 US gal
- Minimum group: 8
- Care: easy
- Verified: 2026-10-30
- Summary: Zebra danios, Danio rerio, are the small striped fish from Indian and Bangladeshi floodplains, and they are also the zebrafish of the lab. The husbandry point Seriously Fish bothers to measure is length. An active school needs a base of 90 × 30 cm, about 21 US gallons. A 20-gallon tank, even the long one, is 30 inches. Ninety centimetres is about 35 inches. The fish is peaceful. The tank people usually offer is short.
- Sources:
  - Seriously Fish: https://www.seriouslyfish.com/species/danio-rerio/
  - FishBase: https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Danio-rerio.html
- Size pages: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/zebra-danio/10-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/zebra-danio/29-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/zebra-danio/40-gallon

### Harlequin rasbora (Trigonostigma heteromorpha)

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/harlequin-rasbora
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/harlequin-rasbora
- Temperature: 21–28 °C (70–82 °F)
- pH: 5–7.5
- Hardness: 1–12 dGH
- Adult size: 45 mm (1.8 in)
- Minimum tank: 14 US gal
- Minimum group: 8
- Care: easy
- Verified: 2026-10-30
- Summary: The harlequin is Trigonostigma heteromorpha, the pink fish with the black wedge, formerly Rasbora heteromorpha. It has been in the hobby since the early 1900s and it is now a farmed fish. Seriously Fish wants a school of at least eight in a tank with a 60 cm base, softer and more acidic water than a platy or a guppy wants, and no drama. The interesting part of the breeding is that they stick the eggs under a leaf, upside down.
- Sources:
  - Seriously Fish: https://www.seriouslyfish.com/species/trigonostigma-heteromorpha/
  - FishBase: https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Trigonostigma-heteromorpha
- Size pages: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/harlequin-rasbora/10-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/harlequin-rasbora/20-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/harlequin-rasbora/29-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/harlequin-rasbora/40-gallon

### Bristlenose pleco (Ancistrus sp. (3))

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/bristlenose-pleco
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/bristlenose-pleco
- Temperature: 21.5–26.5 °C (70.7–79.7 °F)
- pH: 5.8–7.2
- Hardness: not stated
- Adult size: 125 mm (4.9 in)
- Minimum tank: Kathy Jinkings, PlanetCatfish Catfish of the Month, December 1998: a thirty-inch tank for one pair, a four-foot tank for two or three pairs, and nothing smaller as a permanent home. No gallon figure is stated, and this site does not invent one.
- Minimum group: 1
- Care: easy
- Verified: 2026-10-30
- Summary: The bristlenose pleco in a pet shop is not a species anyone has pinned down. PlanetCatfish lists it as Ancistrus sp. (3): a captive-bred fish, possibly a hybrid, that cannot be traced to a river. It is not the common pleco that outgrows a living room. It is a 4.9-inch standard-length loricariid that wants a cave, a current, and vegetables. The label Ancistrus cirrhosus on the bag is a habit, not an identification.
- Sources:
  - PlanetCatfish Cat-eLog: https://www.planetcatfish.com/ancistrus_sp(3)
  - PlanetCatfish, Jinkings 1998: https://www.planetcatfish.com/cotm/cotm.php?article_id=112
- Size pages: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/bristlenose-pleco/10-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/bristlenose-pleco/20-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/bristlenose-pleco/29-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/bristlenose-pleco/40-gallon

### Honey gourami (Trichogaster chuna)

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/honey-gourami
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/honey-gourami
- Temperature: 22–27 °C (72–81 °F)
- pH: 6–7.5
- Hardness: 2–15 dGH
- Adult size: 55 mm (2.2 in)
- Minimum tank: 14 US gal
- Minimum group: 4
- Care: beginner
- Verified: 2026-10-30
- Summary: The honey gourami is Trichogaster chuna, a small labyrinth fish from vegetated, sluggish water in the Ganges and Brahmaputra systems. The fish for sale are farmed, including red and golden strains. Seriously Fish's adult size is 55 mm standard length. FishBase lists 13.7 cm total length, which this site does not believe is usable until someone reconciles it. Plan for the 55 mm fish, a quiet tank, and a group of four to six.
- Sources:
  - Seriously Fish: https://www.seriouslyfish.com/species/trichogaster-chuna/
  - FishBase: https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Trichogaster-chuna.html
- Size pages: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/honey-gourami/10-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/honey-gourami/20-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/honey-gourami/29-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/honey-gourami/40-gallon

### Cardinal tetra (Paracheirodon axelrodi)

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/cardinal-tetra
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/cardinal-tetra
- Temperature: 23–29 °C (73–84 °F)
- pH: 3.5–7.5
- Hardness: 1–12 dGH
- Adult size: 35 mm (1.4 in)
- Minimum tank: 14 US gal
- Minimum group: 8
- Care: easy
- Verified: 2026-10-31
- Summary: Cardinal tetra (Paracheirodon axelrodi) is in the family Acestrorhamphidae. FishBase places it in South America: Upper Orinoco and Negro River basins. The aquarium range used by this checker is the Seriously Fish profile: 73–84°F, pH 3.5–7.5, 35 mm SL. That base is 60 cm. A standard 10-gallon tank is 20 inches, about 51 cm, so it is short of the published footprint even before the gallons are counted.
- Sources:
  - Seriously Fish: https://www.seriouslyfish.com/species/paracheirodon-axelrodi/
  - FishBase: https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Paracheirodon-axelrodi.html
- Size pages: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/cardinal-tetra/10-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/cardinal-tetra/20-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/cardinal-tetra/29-gallon, https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/cardinal-tetra/40-gallon

### Green neon tetra (Paracheirodon simulans)

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/green-neon-tetra
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/green-neon-tetra
- Temperature: 24–27 °C (75–81 °F)
- pH: 3–6.5
- Hardness: 1–8 dGH
- Adult size: 25 mm (1 in)
- Minimum tank: 11 US gal
- Minimum group: not stated
- Care: moderate
- Verified: 2026-10-31
- Summary: Green neon tetra (Paracheirodon simulans) is in the family Acestrorhamphidae. FishBase places it in South America: Upper Negro and Orinoco River basins. The aquarium range used by this checker is the Seriously Fish profile: 75–81°F, pH 3–6.5, 25 mm SL. That base is 45 cm, short enough that a standard 20-inch (10-gallon) tank can cover the length. Volume and the group size are the remaining constraints.

- Summary: Black ruby barb (Pethia nigrofasciata) is in the family Cyprinidae. FishBase places it in Asia: restricted to forest streams from the Kelani to Nilwala basins in Sri Lanka. - Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/red-phantom-tetra
- Temperature: 20–28 °C (68–82 °F)
- pH: 4.5–7.5
- Hardness: 1–12 dGH
- Adult size: 35 mm (1.4 in)
- Minimum tank: 19 US gal
- Minimum group: 8
- Care: easy
- Verified: 2026-11-03
- Summary: Red phantom tetra (Megalamphodus sweglesi) is in the family Acestrorhamphidae. FishBase places it in South America: Orinoco River basin. The aquarium range used by this checker is the Seriously Fish profile: 68–82°F, pH 4.5–7.5, 35 mm SL. That base is 80 cm. A standard 10-gallon tank is 20 inches, about 51 cm, so it is short of the published footprint even before the gallons are counted.
- Sources:
  - Seriously Fish: https://www.seriouslyfish.com/species/hyphessobrycon-sweglesi/

- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/flag-cichlid
- Temperature: 24–28 °C (75–82 °F)
- pH: 6–8
- Hardness: 0–5 dGH
- Adult size: 100 mm (3.9 in)
- Minimum tank: 36 US gal
- Minimum group: not stated
- Care: moderate
- Verified: 2026-11-07
- Summary: Flag cichlid (Mesonauta festivus) is in the family Cichlidae. FishBase places it in South America: Paraná River basin, in the Paraguay River drainage in Brazil and Paraguay; Amazon River basin, in the Guaporé (Brazil and Bolivia), Madre de Dios (Peru), Mamoré (Bolivia), Jamari and Tapajós (Brazil) River drainages. The aquarium range used by this checker is the Seriously Fish profile: 75–82°F, pH 6–8, 100 mm SL. That base is 120 cm. A standard 10-gallon tank is 20 inches, about 51 cm, so it is short of the published footprint even before the gallons are counted.
- Sources:
  - Seriously Fish: https://www.seriouslyfish.com/species/mesonauta-festivus/
  - FishBase: https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Mesonauta-festivus.html

### Amano shrimp (Caridina multidentata)

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/amano-shrimp
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/amano-shrimp
- Temperature: 20–26 °C (68–78.8 °F)
- pH: not stated
- Hardness: not stated
- Adult size: 35 mm (1.4 in)
- Minimum tank: No gallon or length minimum is printed in the sources used here. None is invented.
- Minimum group: not stated
- Care: unrated
- Verified: 2026-11-10
- Summary: Amano shrimp (Caridina multidentata) are freshwater shrimp from Japan and Taiwan. Adults live in rivers and the larvae must reach the sea. Ohara et al. (2024) give 25–35 mm and tested breeding at 20–26°C. They are prey for any fish scored as eating adult shrimp. No pH range is on file.
- Sources:
  - Ohara et al. 2024: https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/aquaticanimals/2024/0/2024_AA2024-5/_pdf/-char/en

### Channeled apple snail (Pomacea canaliculata)

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/channeled-apple-snail
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/channeled-apple-snail
- Temperature: 18–25 °C (64.4–77 °F)
- pH: not stated
- Hardness: not stated
- Adult size: 75 mm (3 in)
- Minimum tank: No gallon or length minimum is printed in the sources used here. None is invented.
- Minimum group: not stated
- Care: unrated
- Verified: 2026-11-10
- Summary: Channeled apple snails (Pomacea canaliculata) are large freshwater snails. The USFWS summary quotes a shell up to 75 mm wide in the usual range, and a temperature preference of 18–25°C. They eat plants, and a care reference reports that they also eat other snails. They are Not compatible with other snails in this set.

- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/spike-topped-apple-snail

- Minimum group: not stated
- Care: unrated
- Verified: 2026-11-10
- Summary: Spike-topped apple snails (Pomacea diffusa) are the mystery snails of the trade. The USFWS summary quotes a shell 40–70 mm high. The temperature used here is 18–28°C from an apple-snail care guide, not a species experiment, and that limit is named on the page. They are not scored as snail-eaters. At 70 mm they are above the small-snail cutoff.

- Care: unrated
- Verified: 2026-11-10
- Summary: Giant apple snails (Pomacea maculata) are very large freshwater snails, up to 165 mm shell height in the USFWS summary. The tolerance figures used here are 15.2–36.6°C and pH 4.0–10.5, from Ramakrishnan (2007) as quoted in that summary. They are tolerance limits, not a target. At this size they are not treated as cherry-shrimp prey.

- Care: unrated
- Verified: 2026-11-10
- Summary: Florida apple snails (Pomacea paludosa) are 60 mm snails in the USFWS summary. The temperature used here is 18–28°C from an apple-snail care guide because the species summary does not print its own numeric band. That gap is on the page. They are above the small-snail cutoff.
- Sources:
  - USFWS ERSS: https://www.fws.gov/sites/default/files/documents/Ecological-Risk-Screening-Summary-Florida-Applesnail.pdf

### Indian apple snail (Pila globosa)

- Species: https://tankmatematch.com/species/indian-apple-snail
- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/indian-apple-snail
- Temperature: 18–28 °C (64.4–82.4 °F)
- pH: not stated
- Hardness: not stated
- Adult size: 60 mm (2.4 in)
- Minimum tank: No gallon or length minimum is printed in the sources used here. None is invented.
- Minimum group: not stated
- Care: unrated
- Verified: 2026-11-10
- Summary: Indian apple snails (Pila globosa) are 4–6 cm snails that use both water and dry ground. The USFWS summary quotes lethal exposures at 10°C, 20°C, and 40°C. The 18–28°C band on this page is the apple-snail care guide, and the page says so. Pairing one with a fully aquatic animal is Caution because the snail needs land, not because it is scored as eating the fish.
- Sources:

- Tank mates: https://tankmatematch.com/tank-mates/new-zealand-mudsnail
- Temperature: 0–34 °C (32–93.2 °F)

- Minimum group: not stated
- Care: unrated
- Verified: 2026-11-10
- Summary: New Zealand mudsnails (Potamopyrgus antipodarum) are tiny invasive snails, to 12 mm in their native range and often 4–6 mm in the Great Lakes.
